relations.subject: server:bucket
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate, applied to a newly-minted object
relations.evidence: Every created bucket is automatically given a default scope, and within it, a default collection. Each is named **\_default**.

relations.subject: server:default-scope-collection
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - extraction-layer predicate already minted by the Capella twin, not yet promoted
relations.evidence: This allows a simple seamless migration from a Cluster/Bucket/Document model to a Cluster/Bucket/Scope/Collection/Document model without concern to any reorganization.

relations.subject: service:eventing-service
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - extraction-layer predicate already minted by the Capella twin, not yet promoted
relations.evidence: The Eventing Service can be used to quickly and efficiently migrate a bucket into a set of collections. An example scriptlet [ConvertBucketToCollections](eventing-handler-ConvertBucketToCollections.md) has been provided to demonstrate the migration of the `beer-sample` data set from a bucket paradigm to a collection paradigm.

relations.subject: eventing:eventing-storage
relations.evidence: If we put the put 'Eventing Storage' (in collections) in the same bucket as with data with non 100% residency the Evening performance can easily drop by a factor of five (5) or more.

relations.subject: eventing:eventing-storage
relations.evidence: Typically the overhead of the Eventing housekeeping area "Eventing Storage" is quite small, just 1024 documents per Function and occasional check point documents. However if Timers are used the size of this collection can grow to about 1K bytes x number of active timers (_for 1M active timers this is 1.5G bytes_). As such the enclosing bucket holding the 'Eventing Storage' needs to be sized appropriately.

relations.subject: server:keyspace
relations.evidence: Increased efficiency of indexing, due to the Data Service being able to provide documents from specific collections to the Index Service.

relations.subject: server:keyspace
relations.evidence: Operations such as query, XDCR, and backup and restore.

relations.subject: server:keyspace
relations.evidence: For complete details on how to set up your keyspaces refer to [creating buckets](../manage/manage-buckets/create-bucket.md) and [creating scopes and collections](#manage:manage-scopes-and-collections/manage-scopes-and-collections.add).

relations.subject: eventing:bucket-to-collections-migration
relations.evidence: An example scriptlet [ConvertBucketToCollections](eventing-handler-ConvertBucketToCollections.md) has been provided to demonstrate the migration of the `beer-sample` data set from a bucket paradigm to a collection paradigm.

Round 8's extraction of the twin characterized both of that page's links as broken; in fact only the second one is broken on both trees, and the first ('creating buckets') resolves correctly to a working markdown relative link on THIS page (../manage/manage-buckets/create-bucket.md) while remaining broken only on the Capella twin. The adoc-to-md conversion pipeline issue is narrower and more mixed than round 8's record states.

cross_component_finding: This page corroborates the Capella twin's central finding using server:-namespaced concepts instead of capella:-namespaced ones: Eventing introduces no new structural primitive for the bucket/scope/collection hierarchy on the Server side either - it fully adopts server:bucket/server:scope/server:keyspace, including the _default/_default fallback, and its only novel contribution is functional (using a Function as a one-time migration engine). The same 5x-or-worse throughput warning for co-locating a low-residency Eventing Storage collection recurs here with server-specific vocabulary, corroborating rather than contradicting the twin.
